- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.2) — model tends to lag or overshoot upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.16) — model fails to capture downward pressure or mean reversion.
- Avoid overreacting to recent spikes — model often overshoots after a sharp rise, especially if sentiment is positive.
- Mean-reversion bias: model frequently overcorrects after strong moves, underestimating the return to prior levels.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are consistently too low in the early part of the forecast window, especially when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model tends to smooth out extremes — underestimates upward moves and overestimates downward ones.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model should increase forecast slope — current model underweights sentiment-driven momentum.
